entries.claim: The phase-close queue assertion is performed on an unlocked, pre-transition snapshot, so it does not assert that the queue is empty when the phase actually closes.
entries.failure_scenario: A concurrent `/cad-capture` (or any writer) appends an item to CAPTURE.md after `readQueue()` reads an empty file but before `runTransition` flips ROADMAP.md. `phase-done` then returns `capture: { substantive: 0, items: [] }` and closes the phase although CAPTURE.md contains a live user queue entry at close. The new report can therefore falsely certify the exact invariant this change is intended to surface.

counter_evidence.note: The ordering claim is true - the read is deliberately before the transition and takes no lock - but the severity is not high. The same block states the consequence: `a non-empty queue is a named problem and never a refusal, because a phase completion is a fact about the work, not about this file`, and the close path has no arm that reads `capture` back. So the field gates nothing, deletes nothing and truncates nothing; the raced queue entry stays in CAPTURE.md and the next capture-check or cad-health reads it. The loss is one stale report line in a single-operator CLI, not a certified-empty queue that ate an item.
